nodes.name: Ambient measurable space and sub-sigma-algebra
nodes.statement: Let $(X, \MCX)$ be a measurable space, let $\MCB$ be a sub $\sigma$-algebra of $\MCX$.

nodes.label: def:lebesgue-cond-exp

nodes.name: Characterisation of the Lebesgue conditional expectation
nodes.statement: {} If $f : X \to [0, \infty]$ is a $\MCX$-measurable function, then $\mu[f | \MCB]$ is the $\mu$-ae unique $\MCB$-measurable function $X \to [0, \infty]$ such that \[\int_B \mu[f | \MCB]\ \partial\mu = \int_B f\ \partial\mu\] for all $B \in \MCB$.
assumptions: $f : X \to [0, \infty]$ is a $\MCX$-measurable function
conclusions: $\mu[f | \MCB]$ is the $\mu$-ae unique $\MCB$-measurable function $X \to [0, \infty]$ such that \[\int_B \mu[f | \MCB]\ \partial\mu = \int_B f\ \partial\mu\] for all $B \in \MCB$
nodes.statement_short: $\mu[f|\MCB]$ is the a.e.-unique $\MCB$-measurable function with the same integrals as $f$ over every $B\in\MCB$.
nodes.label: lem:lebesgue-cond-exp-char

nodes.name: Juxtaposition
nodes.statement: {} Let $E$ and $S$ be sets. Let $\Delta\in\mathcal{P}(S)$, and let $\omega\in E^S$. We define \begin{align} \juxtBy{\omega} : E^\Delta&\to E^S\\ \zeta&\mapsto \delta\mapsto\begin{cases} \zeta_\delta & \delta\in\Delta\\ \omega_\delta & \delta\notin\Delta \end{cases} \end{align} to be the \textbf{juxtaposition of $\zeta$ and $\omega$} (for each $\zeta\in E^\Delta$).
nodes.statement_short: $\juxtBy{\omega}\zeta$ agrees with $\zeta$ on $\Delta$ and with $\omega$ off $\Delta$.
nodes.label: def:juxtaposition

nodes.name: Juxtaposition map signature
nodes.statement: \juxtBy{\omega} : E^\Delta&\to E^S

nodes.name: Juxtaposition map formula
nodes.statement: \zeta&\mapsto \delta\mapsto\begin{cases} \zeta_\delta & \delta\in\Delta\\ \omega_\delta & \delta\notin\Delta \end{cases}

nodes.name: Cylinder events
nodes.statement: {} Let $(E,\mathcal{E})$ be a measurable space, and let $S$ be a set. Then, \begin{align} \mathcal{F}:\mathcal{P}(S)&\to \set{\text{sigma algebras on } E^S}\\ \Delta&\mapsto \sigma(\{\text{proj}_\delta:E^S\to E\mid \delta\in \Delta\}) \end{align} defines the \textbf{cylinder events in }$\Delta$ (for each $\Delta\in\mathcal{P}(S)$), where each $\text{proj}_\delta$ is the coordinate projection at coordinate $\delta$.
nodes.statement_short: $\mathcal{F}_\Delta$ is the sigma-algebra on $E^S$ generated by the coordinate projections indexed by $\Delta$.
nodes.label: def:cylinder-event

nodes.name: Cylinder event map signature
nodes.statement: \mathcal{F}:\mathcal{P}(S)&\to \set{\text{sigma algebras on } E^S}

nodes.name: Cylinder event map formula
nodes.statement: \Delta&\mapsto \sigma(\{\text{proj}_\delta:E^S\to E\mid \delta\in \Delta\})

nodes.name: Kernel
nodes.statement: {} Let $(X,\MCX)$ and $(Y,\mathcal{Y})$ be measurable spaces. Then, \[\text{Ker}_{\mathcal{Y},\MCX}:=\left\{\pi:\MCX\times Y\to[0,\infty]~\middle\vert~ \forall y\in Y,\pi(\cdot\mid y)\in\mathfrak{M}(X,\MCX);~\forall A\in\MCX,\pi(A\mid\cdot)\text{ is }\mathcal{Y}\text{-measurable}\right\}\] defines the set of \textbf{kernels from $\mathcal{Y}$ to $\MCX$}, where $\mathfrak{M}(X,\MCX)$ is the space of measures on $X$.
nodes.statement_short: A kernel is a map $\pi(\cdot|y)$ that is a measure for each $y$ and measurable in $y$ for each set.
nodes.label: def:kernel

nodes.name: Markov kernel
nodes.statement: {} Let $(X,\MCX)$ and $(Y,\mathcal{Y})$ be measurable spaces. We say that $\pi\in\text{Ker}_{\mathcal{Y},\MCX}$ is a \textbf{Markov kernel} iff $\pi(X\mid \cdot)=1$.
nodes.label: def:markov-ker

nodes.name: Fixed kernel $\pi$
nodes.statement: Let $\pi \in \text{Ker}_{\MCB, \MCX}$.

nodes.name: Proper kernel
nodes.statement: {} $\pi$ is \textbf{proper} iff $\pi(A\cap B\mid x)=\pi(A\mid x)\cdot\mathbf{1}_B(x)$ for all $A\in\MCX$, $B\in\MCB$ and $x\in X$.
differentia: $\pi(A\cap B\mid x)=\pi(A\mid x)\cdot\mathbf{1}_B(x)$ for all $A\in\MCX$, $B\in\MCB$ and $x\in X$
nodes.label: def:proper-ker

nodes.name: Lebesgue integral characterisation of proper kernels
nodes.statement: {} If $\pi$ is proper, then \[\int f(x) g(x)\ \pi(dx\mid x_0) = g(x_0)\int f(x)\ \pi(dx\mid x_0)\] for all $x_0 \in X$ and functions $f, g : X \to [0, \infty]$ such that $f$ is $\MCX$-measurable, $g$ is $\MCB$-measurable.
assumptions: $\pi$ is proper
for all $x_0 \in X$ and functions $f, g : X \to [0, \infty]$ such that $f$ is $\MCX$-measurable, $g$ is $\MCB$-measurable
conclusions: \[\int f(x) g(x)\ \pi(dx\mid x_0) = g(x_0)\int f(x)\ \pi(dx\mid x_0)\]
nodes.statement_short: A proper kernel pulls out $\MCB$-measurable nonnegative factors from its integrals.
nodes.label: lem:proper-ker-lintegral

nodes.name: Integral characterisation of proper kernels
nodes.statement: {} If $\pi$ is a proper Markov kernel and $g$ is a bounded function, then \[\int f(x) g(x)\ \pi(dx\mid x_0) = g(x_0)\int f(x)\ \pi(dx\mid x_0)\] for all $x_0 \in X$ and functions $f, g : X \to \R$ such that $f$ is bounded $\MCX$-measurable and $g$ is bounded $\MCB$-measurable.
assumptions: $\pi$ is a proper Markov kernel and $g$ is a bounded function
for all $x_0 \in X$ and functions $f, g : X \to \R$ such that $f$ is bounded $\MCX$-measurable and $g$ is bounded $\MCB$-measurable
conclusions: \[\int f(x) g(x)\ \pi(dx\mid x_0) = g(x_0)\int f(x)\ \pi(dx\mid x_0)\]
nodes.statement_short: Bounded real version: a proper Markov kernel pulls out bounded $\MCB$-measurable factors.
nodes.label: lem:proper-ker-integral

nodes.name: Conditional expectation kernel
nodes.statement: {} Let $\mu\in\mathfrak{M}(X,\MCX)$. Then, $\pi\in\text{Ker}_{\MCB,\MCX}$ is a \textbf{conditional expectation kernel for $\mu$} if $\mu(A\mid \MCB)=\pi(A\mid\cdot)$ $\mu$-a.e.
nodes.label: def:cond-exp-ker

nodes.name: Lebesgue integral characterisation of proper conditional expectation kernels
nodes.statement: If $\pi \in \text{Ker}_{\MCB, \MCX}$ is a conditional expectation kernel for $\mu$, then \[\mu[f\mid \MCB] = \int f(x)\ \pi(\partial x\mid\cdot)\ \mu\text{-a.e.}\] for all $\MCX$-measurable functions $f : X \to [0, \infty]$.
assumptions: $\pi \in \text{Ker}_{\MCB, \MCX}$ is a conditional expectation kernel for $\mu$
for all $\MCX$-measurable functions $f : X \to [0, \infty]$
nodes.statement_short: A conditional expectation kernel computes the conditional expectation of nonnegative measurable functions a.e.
nodes.label: lem:cond-exp-proper-ker-lintegral

nodes.name: Characterisation of proper conditional expectation kernels
nodes.statement: Let $\mu\in\mathfrak{M}(X,\MCX)$ be a finite measure and let $\pi\in\text{Ker}_{\MCB,\MCX}$ be a proper kernel. Then, $$\pi \text{ is a conditional expectation kernel for }\mu \iff \mu\pi = \mu$$
nodes.origin_citation: Georgii, Gibbs Measures and Phase Transitions, Remark 1.20
assumptions: Let $\mu\in\mathfrak{M}(X,\MCX)$ be a finite measure and let $\pi\in\text{Ker}_{\MCB,\MCX}$ be a proper kernel.
conclusions: $$\pi \text{ is a conditional expectation kernel for }\mu \iff \mu\pi = \mu$$
equivalent_conditions: \pi \text{ is a conditional expectation kernel for }\mu
nodes.statement_short: A proper kernel is a conditional expectation kernel for finite $\mu$ iff $\mu$ is invariant under it.
nodes.label: lem:cond-exp-proper-ker-bind

nodes.name: Proof of LP6
nodes.statement: By the characterisation of conditional expectation, $$\pi \text{ is a conditional expectation kernel for }\mu \iff \forall A \in \MCX, \forall B \in \MCB, \mu(A \inter B) = \int_B \pi(A|\cdot)\ \partial\mu$$ By properness of $\pi$, $$\int_B \pi(A|\cdot)\ \partial\mu = \mu\pi(A \inter B)$$ Hence \begin{align} \pi \text{ is a cond. exp. kernel with respect to }\mu & \iff \forall A \in \MCX, \forall B \in \MCB, \mu(A \inter B) = \mu\pi(A \inter B) \\ & \iff \forall A \in \MCX, \mu(A) = \mu\pi(A) \\ & \iff \mu = \mu\pi \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Rewrite the characterisation of conditional expectation using properness, then reduce to $\mu=\mu\pi$.

nodes.name: Apply the characterisation of conditional expectation
nodes.statement: By the characterisation of conditional expectation, $$\pi \text{ is a conditional expectation kernel for }\mu \iff \forall A \in \MCX, \forall B \in \MCB, \mu(A \inter B) = \int_B \pi(A|\cdot)\ \partial\mu$$
nodes.statement_short: Apply the characterisation of conditional expectation

nodes.name: Rewrite the integral by properness of $\pi$
nodes.statement: By properness of $\pi$, $$\int_B \pi(A|\cdot)\ \partial\mu = \mu\pi(A \inter B)$$
nodes.statement_short: Rewrite the integral by properness of $\pi$

nodes.name: Chain of equivalences down to $\mu=\mu\pi$
nodes.statement: Hence \begin{align} \pi \text{ is a cond. exp. kernel with respect to }\mu & \iff \forall A \in \MCX, \forall B \in \MCB, \mu(A \inter B) = \mu\pi(A \inter B) \\ & \iff \forall A \in \MCX, \mu(A) = \mu\pi(A) \\ & \iff \mu = \mu\pi \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Chain of equivalences down to $\mu=\mu\pi$

nodes.name: Equivalence chain for conditional expectation kernels
nodes.statement: \pi \text{ is a cond. exp. kernel with respect to }\mu & \iff \forall A \in \MCX, \forall B \in \MCB, \mu(A \inter B) = \mu\pi(A \inter B) \\ & \iff \forall A \in \MCX, \mu(A) = \mu\pi(A) \\ & \iff \mu = \mu\pi

nodes.name: Specification
nodes.statement: {} A {\bf specification} is a family of kernels $\gamma : \Finset S \to \Ker_{\mathcal{F}_{S\setminus\Lambda}, \mathcal{E}^S}$ which is {\bf consistent}, in the sense that \[\forall \Lambda_1, \Lambda_2 \in \Finset(S), \Lambda_1 \subseteq \Lambda_2 \implies \gamma_{\Lambda_1} \circ_k \gamma_{\Lambda_2} = \gamma_{\Lambda_2}\]
nodes.statement_short: A consistent family of kernels $\gamma_\Lambda$ indexed by finite $\Lambda\subseteq S$ with $\gamma_{\Lambda_1}\circ\gamma_{\Lambda_2}=\gamma_{\Lambda_2}$.
nodes.label: def:spec

nodes.name: Standing parameter set and state space
nodes.statement: All specifications will be with parameter set $S$ and state space $(E, \mathcal{E})$ in this chapter.

nodes.name: Independent specification
nodes.statement: {} A specification $\gamma$ is \textbf{independent} iff \[\forall \Lambda_1, \Lambda_2 \in \Finset(S), \gamma_{\Lambda_1} \circ_k \gamma_{\Lambda_2} = \gamma_{\Lambda_1\cup\Lambda_2}\]
nodes.label: def:indep-spec

nodes.name: Markov specification
nodes.statement: {} A specification $\gamma$ is a \textbf{Markov specification} iff $\gamma_\Lambda$ is a probability kernel for every $\Lambda \in \Finset(S)$.
nodes.label: def:markov-spec

nodes.name: Proper specification
nodes.statement: {} A specification $\gamma$ is \textbf{proper} iff the kernel $\gamma_\Lambda$ is proper for every $\Lambda \in \Finset(S)$.
nodes.label: def:proper-spec

nodes.name: Gibbs measures
nodes.statement: Given a specification $\gamma$, a \textbf{Gibbs measures specified by $\gamma$} is a measure $\nu \in \mathfrak{M}(E^S, \mathcal{E}^S)$ such that $\gamma_\Lambda(A|\cdot)$ is a conditional expectation kernel for $\nu$ for all $A \in \mathcal E^S$ and $\Lambda \in \Finset(S)$.
differentia: $\gamma_\Lambda(A|\cdot)$ is a conditional expectation kernel for $\nu$ for all $A \in \mathcal E^S$ and $\Lambda \in \Finset(S)$
nodes.label: def:gibbs-meas

nodes.statement: Let $S$ be a set, $(E, \mathcal{E})$ be a measurable space and $\nu$ a measure on $E$.

nodes.name: Product probability measure
nodes.statement: {} Let $I$ be a set. Suppose for each $i\in I$ that $(\Omega_i,\MCB_i,P_i)$ is a probability space. Then, $P:=\bigotimes_{i\in I}P_i$ is a well-defined product probability measure on $\prod_{i\in I}\Omega_i$.
nodes.label: def:product-probability-measure

nodes.name: Modifier
nodes.statement: {} A {\bf modifier of $\gamma$} is a family \[\rho : \Finset(S) \to \Omega \to [0, \infty[\] such that the corresponding family of kernels $\rho\gamma$ is a specification.

nodes.name: Proof of LP13
nodes.statement: For all $\Lambda \in \Finset(S)$, $A \in \mathcal E^S$, $B \in \mathcal{F}_{S\setminus\Lambda}$, $\eta : S \to E$, we want to prove $$(\rho\gamma)_\Lambda(A \inter B | \eta) = 1_B(\eta) (\rho\gamma)_\Lambda(A B | \eta)$$ Expanding out, this is equivalent to $$\int_{\zeta \in A \inter B} \rho_\Lambda(\zeta)\ d(\gamma_\Lambda(\eta)) = 1_B(\eta) \int_{\zeta \in A} \rho_\Lambda(\zeta)\ d(\gamma_\Lambda(\eta))$$ which is true by Lemma \ref{lem:proper-ker-lintegral} with $f = 1_A\rho_\Lambda$, $g = 1_B$.
nodes.statement_short: Expand the modified kernel as an integral and apply the Lebesgue integral characterisation of proper kernels with $f=1_A\rho_\Lambda$, $g=1_B$.

nodes.name: Every specification is a modification of some ISSSD
nodes.statement: If $E$ is countable, $\nu$ is the counting measure and $\gamma$ is any specification, then $$\rho_\Lambda(\eta) = \gamma_\Lambda(\{\sigma_\Lambda = \eta_\Lambda\} | \eta)$$ is a modifier from $\ISSSD(\nu)$ to $\gamma$.
nodes.origin_citation: Georgii, Gibbs Measures and Phase Transitions, Remark 1.28.5
assumptions: $E$ is countable
$\nu$ is the counting measure
$\gamma$ is any specification
nodes.statement_short: Over a countable state space, $\rho_\Lambda(\eta)=\gamma_\Lambda(\{\sigma_\Lambda=\eta_\Lambda\}|\eta)$ modifies the counting-measure ISSSD into $\gamma$.
nodes.label: lem:exists-modif-isssd

nodes.name: Characterisation of modifiers
nodes.statement: {} If $\rho$ is a family of measurable densities and $\gamma$ is a proper Markov specification, then TFAE \begin{enumerate} \item $\rho$ is a modifier of $\gamma$ \item For all $\Lambda_1, \Lambda_2$ with $\Lambda_1 \subseteq \Lambda_2$ and all $\eta : S \to E$, we have \[\rho_{\Lambda_2} = \rho_{\Lambda_1}\cdot (\gamma_{\Lambda_1} \rho_{\Lambda_2}) \quad \gamma_{\Lambda_2}(\cdot|\eta)\text{-a.e.}\] \end{enumerate} Georgii's (1.30) is the $\lambda$-specification case, and assumes $\lambda_\Lambda\rho_\Lambda=1$ from the start.
nodes.origin_citation: Georgii, Gibbs Measures and Phase Transitions, Proposition 1.30.1
assumptions: $\rho$ is a family of measurable densities and $\gamma$ is a proper Markov specification
conclusions: TFAE \begin{enumerate} \item $\rho$ is a modifier of $\gamma$ \item For all $\Lambda_1, \Lambda_2$ with $\Lambda_1 \subseteq \Lambda_2$ and all $\eta : S \to E$, we have \[\rho_{\Lambda_2} = \rho_{\Lambda_1}\cdot (\gamma_{\Lambda_1} \rho_{\Lambda_2}) \quad \gamma_{\Lambda_2}(\cdot|\eta)\text{-a.e.}\] \end{enumerate}
equivalent_conditions: For all $\Lambda_1, \Lambda_2$ with $\Lambda_1 \subseteq \Lambda_2$ and all $\eta : S \to E$, we have \[\rho_{\Lambda_2} = \rho_{\Lambda_1}\cdot (\gamma_{\Lambda_1} \rho_{\Lambda_2}) \quad \gamma_{\Lambda_2}(\cdot|\eta)\text{-a.e.}\]
nodes.statement_short: For a proper Markov specification, $\rho$ is a modifier iff $\rho_{\Lambda_2}=\rho_{\Lambda_1}(\gamma_{\Lambda_1}\rho_{\Lambda_2})$ a.e. for nested $\Lambda_1\subseteq\Lambda_2$.

nodes.name: Characterisation of modifiers of independent specifications
nodes.statement: {} If $\rho$ is a family of measurable densities, $\gamma$ is a proper Markov independent specification, and $\gamma_\Lambda(\rho_\Lambda)=1$ for all $\Lambda$, then TFAE \begin{enumerate} \item $\rho$ is a modifier of $\gamma$ \item For all $\Lambda_1, \Lambda_2$ with $\Lambda_1 \subseteq \Lambda_2$, $\eta : S \to E$ and $\gamma_{\Lambda_2 \setminus \Lambda_1}(\cdot|\alpha)$-almost all $\eta_2 : S \to E$, we have \[\rho_{\Lambda_2}(\zeta_1)\rho_{\Lambda_1}(\zeta_2) = \rho_{\Lambda_2}(\zeta_2) \rho_{\Lambda_1}(\zeta_1)\] for $\gamma_{\Lambda_1}(\cdot|\eta_2) \times \gamma_{\Lambda_1}(\cdot|\eta_2)$-almost all $(\zeta_1, \zeta_2)$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.origin_citation: Georgii, Gibbs Measures and Phase Transitions, Proposition 1.30.2
assumptions: $\rho$ is a family of measurable densities, $\gamma$ is a proper Markov independent specification, and $\gamma_\Lambda(\rho_\Lambda)=1$ for all $\Lambda$
conclusions: TFAE \begin{enumerate} \item $\rho$ is a modifier of $\gamma$ \item For all $\Lambda_1, \Lambda_2$ with $\Lambda_1 \subseteq \Lambda_2$, $\eta : S \to E$ and $\gamma_{\Lambda_2 \setminus \Lambda_1}(\cdot|\alpha)$-almost all $\eta_2 : S \to E$, we have \[\rho_{\Lambda_2}(\zeta_1)\rho_{\Lambda_1}(\zeta_2) = \rho_{\Lambda_2}(\zeta_2) \rho_{\Lambda_1}(\zeta_1)\] for $\gamma_{\Lambda_1}(\cdot|\eta_2) \times \gamma_{\Lambda_1}(\cdot|\eta_2)$-almost all $(\zeta_1, \zeta_2)$. \end{enumerate}
equivalent_conditions: For all $\Lambda_1, \Lambda_2$ with $\Lambda_1 \subseteq \Lambda_2$, $\eta : S \to E$ and $\gamma_{\Lambda_2 \setminus \Lambda_1}(\cdot|\alpha)$-almost all $\eta_2 : S \to E$, we have \[\rho_{\Lambda_2}(\zeta_1)\rho_{\Lambda_1}(\zeta_2) = \rho_{\Lambda_2}(\zeta_2) \rho_{\Lambda_1}(\zeta_1)\] for $\gamma_{\Lambda_1}(\cdot|\eta_2) \times \gamma_{\Lambda_1}(\cdot|\eta_2)$-almost all $(\zeta_1, \zeta_2)$.
nodes.statement_short: For a proper Markov independent specification with normalised densities, $\rho$ is a modifier iff a cross-ratio symmetry holds a.e.
nodes.label: prop:modif-indep-char

nodes.name: Premodifier
nodes.statement: A family of measurable functions $h_\Lambda : (S \to E) \to [0, \infty[$ is a {\bf premodifier} if $$h_{\Lambda_2}(\zeta)h_{\Lambda_1}(\eta) = h_{\Lambda_1}(\zeta)h_{\Lambda_2}(\eta)$$ for all $\Lambda_1 \subseteq \Lambda_2$ and all $\zeta, \eta : S \to E$ such that $\zeta_{\Lambda_1^c} = \eta_{\Lambda_1^c}$.
nodes.origin_citation: Georgii, Gibbs Measures and Phase Transitions, Definition 1.31
nodes.statement_short: $h$ is a premodifier if $h_{\Lambda_2}(\zeta)h_{\Lambda_1}(\eta)=h_{\Lambda_1}(\zeta)h_{\Lambda_2}(\eta)$ whenever $\zeta,\eta$ agree off $\Lambda_1$.
nodes.label: def:premodif
